# Dark stage talk — Style Prompt

> A launch film where the interface is the star: a near-black stage with a soft lift of cool light, one glowing accent caret that types a calm line, and then the problem shown as generated UI. Notification cards slide in, files drop, photos fling, all faster and faster while the camera pulls back in log space until the line is buried in hundreds of items. Half-second inserts hammer the numbers home (a red badge climbing, a giant figure locking digit by digit, a storage bar nearly full), and then one decisive beat: everything freezes, flies into a grid, puts itself away to a single accent tile, and the caret types the answer.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

A stage talk-grade film for **software, services and anything that tidies a mess**. There is no physical product and no glass render: the protagonist is the interface (a caret, cards, files, photos, a number). It lives on a dark stage lit by soft, cool light, with **one brand accent** reserved for the single most important element: the caret at the start, the tile at the end.

The style is defined by **precision**: every element snaps to a grid or a beat, every type of element has exactly one motion, and drama comes from contrast: disorder shown as *generated* UI (you never hand-draw the mess, a rule spawns it), one decisive action, then empty space. The opening and the ending rhyme: the same framing, the same caret, a calm line before and the answer after.

Not a glass product render (no physical object), not a screencast (no real operating system, apps, logos or window buttons), not a hologram HUD (no scanlines, no cyan glow), not a chart film (one number at a time, never a dashboard), not a slideshow (nothing just fades in or out).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Stage**: a near-black base (`--latar`) with a radial lift at the upper centre (`--latar-2` mixed 72 % into it, 1500 × 860 px at 50 % 26 %), one large cool glow off-centre at 7 % of `--aksen`, and a soft corner vignette (transparent to 55 %, then 32 % of a darkened background). No grain, no texture.
- **Hairline grid** on a 48 px module, `--teks` at 3 %, every 4th line at 6 %. It is the floor of the inserts and the end; during the pile-up it is never seen.
- **UI kit, all original and drawn in code**:
  - notification card: 1100 × 300 at full size, radius 42, a 150 px app icon (rounded square, radius 38, a category hue with a lighter top-left and a white glyph), a 600 title, a 400 subtitle in `--teks-redup`, a small timestamp ("baru") top right, an optional red badge;
  - file: a 150 × 190 paper sheet with a folded corner (clip-path), grey text lines, a coloured type tag (PDF, XLS, DOC, JPG, ZIP, TXT) and a mono filename underneath (`layout_rev7.pdf`, `foto_kelas_FIX(2).jpg`): the filenames tell the story of the mess;
  - photo: a procedural landscape, 600 × 392, radius 28: a two-stop sky gradient, a pale sun, two mountain ridges darkened from the sky colours;
  - window: a title bar with only a small coloured glyph and a mono title (never traffic-light buttons, menu bars or docks), body of grey row bars or columns of mono numbers.
- **Surfaces**: three steps of raised dark surface (card gradient from `--latar-2` lifted 8 % toward `--teks`, card, window), a 1 px border at 10 % of `--teks`, a 1 px inner top highlight at 8 %, soft drop shadows (black 42 %, 20-24 px offset, 40-48 px blur).
- **Depth**: a 2.5D camera, screen scale `s = 1/(1/zoom − d)` per layer, `d` > 0 near the lens (shrinks faster as the camera pulls back), `d` < 0 far (shrinks slower, its items dimmed by a painted 22 % veil of `--latar`). The first card near the lens is the largest thing on screen (1.5×) and runs off the edge; no blur filters.
- **Light** is a reveal tool: a soft band (a transparent → 16 % `--teks` → transparent gradient, 460 px wide) passes and the tiles it touches turn from 45 % to full.

## 3. Colour logic

- **A cool neutral ladder**: `--latar` the stage, `--latar-2` the cards and panels (with a lighter top step and a darker window step mixed from the two), `--teks` the primary text, `--teks-redup` secondary text, timestamps, mono labels and filenames on windows. Neutrals are slightly blue, never warm.
- **One accent = `--utama`**, saturated and luminous with its own glow. It is the product: the caret (as a line on the stage it uses `--utama-di-latar`), the caption toast's speaking dot, the final tile (filled `--utama`, glyph and year in `--teks-di-utama`). If two things are accent-coloured at once, one is wrong.
- **`--aksen`** is only the faint cool glow on the stage (7 %). It never fills UI.
- **Fixed in every brand**:
  - the problem red (`#f2474f`) for badges and the storage bar, which exists only while the problem exists and never returns after the turn;
  - category codes for app icons and file tags (indigo, violet, green, amber, sky), white glyphs on them;
  - the paper of files (`#dfe1e7`);
  - the photo palettes: sunset (`#d8763f` → `#f7b866`), day (`#6aa2e8` → `#d3e3f6`), dusk (`#57297a` → `#d4648a`), night (`#20305c` → `#5d77aa`), mint (`#a3dccf` → `#5c9ea0`), weighted roughly 3:2:2:2:1, ridges mixed from the sky toward black (far 80 %, near 54 %).
- On a pale brand the stage turns light and the cards stay legible through their border and shadow; on a dark brand the ladder follows the brand's background. Category hues and photos do not change.

## 4. Type

- **`--font-judul`**: the typed headline, Inter 600 at 132 px, line height 150 px, tracking −3.5 %, one line per screen, about 16 characters (it spans half the frame from x 444). The giant number in an insert: Inter 600 at 190 px, tracking −4.5 %, tabular figures, with its unit beside it in `--font-isi` 400 at 64 px, `--teks-redup`.
- **`--font-isi`**: card titles 600 at 64 px and subtitles 400 at 56 px (at full card size), caption toasts 400 at 40 px, the contact chip 600 at 48 px, insert labels 600 at 64 px.
- **Mono** (`--font-kode`, IBM Plex Mono 400, a look token the brand does not replace): the small-caps label above the headline at 40 px with 0.3 em tracking, filenames, window titles, numbers in windows, status values ("0,4 GB lagi").
- **Caption toasts are a UI component**: a bottom-centre pill (92 % of `--latar-2`, 1 px border, soft shadow) with a 14 px accent dot that glows. They name what is piling up in two or three words ("Chat grup angkatan.").
- Typed text is its own caption: never repeat a typed line in a toast. When the brand has no fonts: Inter 600 for headlines, Inter 400/600 for UI; Space Grotesk also suits. A wider brand font needs a shorter line, not a smaller size.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Everything lands on a beat.** Moves start a beat early and land on it, fast-out with one small overshoot (`back.out(1.3)`), then settle immediately. No floaty sine drift; between moves things are still.
- **Typing**: 0.055 s per character for the opening line, faster (0.022 s) for the answer at the end; the caret is solid while typing, then Enter drops it to the next line, where it blinks on a 1.06 s cycle (0.53 s on, 0.53 s off) as the film's metronome.
- **One motion per element type, 0.26-0.36 s**: cards slide in from their nearest edge (640 px × scale, `back.out(1.3)`, 0.32 s), files drop 260 px with a 30° tumble (`back.out(1.8)`, 0.3 s), photos are flung from outside the frame turning 26° and shrinking from 1.3× (`back.out(1.25)`, 0.36 s), windows pop from 0.55× (`back.out(1.5)`, 0.26 s), badges pop from 0 (`back.out(2.2)`, 0.2 s) 0.16 s after their card.
- **Accumulation is a rule, not a layout**: beats of 10, 14, 18, 22 and 26 items after two hand-placed beats, each beat shorter (1.1 → 0.7 s) and its items smaller (spawn scale 1.1 → 0.68), the stagger accelerating within a beat (`(i/n)^0.85`); later beats keep the centre emptier (they fill the ring the pull-back reveals).
- **Captions**: rise 16 px and fade in 0.16 s, hold about 1.5-2 s, retract (scaleX to 0.3 with a fade, 0.14 s). About one every 1.8 s during the pile-up.
- **Inserts**: each lasts about 0.75 s; within one, the value changes every 0.22-0.25 s with a pop (scale 1.3 → 1, 0.14 s). A number from glyph noise scrambles for 0.5 s and locks left to right, one digit per beat, then bounces 1.06 → 1.
- **Disappearing is designed**: toasts retract, an insert collapses CRT-style (scaleY to 0.008 in 0.09 s, then scaleX to 0 in 0.07 s), grid tiles put themselves away a pair of columns per 0.11 s beat (flatten 0.07 s, narrow 0.06 s). Nothing just fades.
- **The snap**: the camera freezes; at once the pile collapses toward the centre (0.3 s, `power3.in`) while the visible photos fly to a 7 × 3 grid in one beat (0.45 s, 0.008 s apart; x on `power2.out`, y on `back.out(1.3)`, so every path bends the same way and none cross).
- **Hold the end** at least 2 s, the caret solid, nothing moving.

## 6. Camera grammar

A vocabulary, not a route. Opening and ending come from the topic.

| Move | Expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Locked frame on a tiny live element (the caret) | intimacy: one thing alive on a screen | the first line; a thought forming; a quiet status |
| Continuous pull-back in log space, accelerating (zoom 1 → 0.27 over about 6 s, `u^1.25`), focus drifting right, roll to −2° | accumulation, the mess growing out of one point | inboxes piling up; costs creeping; a class group exploding with messages |
| Half-second inserts expanding from their source (clip-path open in 0.16 s, one frame early) | overload, too much to read | a badge count; tabs or files open; storage, deadlines, errors |
| Whip pull-out in one beat after an insert (zoom 0.235 → 0.17 in 0.7 s, `expo.out`, roll to +2.4°) | cause and effect at once: the whole mess seen | the scale of the problem before the turn |
| Freeze | time stopped, the decision | the instant before the product acts |
| Near-locked frame while a soft light band sweeps | presentation, the product as hero | a reveal; a sorted grid; a new version |
| Return to the opening framing | rhyme: what changed | the answer typed where the question was; the call to action |

Framing: generous negative space, one focal element, the accent at the focal point. Dutch angle only during disorder. **Transitions are UI expanding or collapsing**: every shot change is an interface element opening into the frame or the frame collapsing into an element.

## 7. Native moves

- **Typed line and living caret.** One calm line typed by the accent caret on an empty stage, Enter, and the caret keeps blinking as the world buries it. *Fits content like:* "Cuma satu album." for a yearbook service; a course title typed before its syllabus floods in; a creator's video idea typed before the comments pile up; the first line of a short story.
- **Generated accumulation.** UI spawned by rule, faster and faster, cards sliding, files dropping, photos flung, while the camera pulls back in log space; toasts name each wave. *Fits content like:* a committee's chat, forms and photos piling up; a shop's orders across three apps; a teacher's ungraded homework; a creator's unanswered DMs.
- **Half-second inserts.** A hard insert per number on the gridded stage: a red badge climbing to 999+, a giant figure scrambling and locking, a storage bar nearly full. *Fits content like:* unread messages; photos received; days to a deadline; a phone's memory; tickets left.
- **Freeze and the snap grid.** Everything stops, the pile collapses, and what matters flies into one grid in a single beat. *Fits content like:* all class photos in one album; a week of posts scheduled; files sorted by client; a menu tidied into categories.
- **Light reveal.** A soft band sweeps across the grid and only what it has passed turns on (glint ≤ 20 %, under 0.7 s). *Fits content like:* a redesigned page; a finished gallery; a course module unlocked; a new price list.
- **Put-away to one tile.** The grid dismantles itself a pair of columns per beat until one tile is left, lit in the accent, and it flies home to the opening framing for the call to action. *Fits content like:* "satu link" for everyone; one app replacing five; focus mode; the one class worth taking.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Raster size.** A layer authored in world coordinates becomes enormous once the camera has pulled back to 0.2. Author each spawn beat in the screen coordinates of its own moment and scale the layer by `s(t)/s(born)`: every bitmap stays about one screen large. Move layers only by transform (`will-change: transform`), never redraw items per frame.
- **Live preview budget.** About 100 items in all (more adds paint chunks the browser re-layerizes every frame); give each spawn beat its own child timeline so the main timeline does not walk hundreds of tweens per frame; skip camera updates for layers not yet born and while an insert covers the pile; hide the pile (`autoAlpha: 0`) under the inserts; keep shadows static and modest (≤ 48 px blur).
- **Translucent depth looks muddy, and costs.** Layer opacity shows everything behind and, on a layer with moving children, forces an extra compositing pass. Dim far items with a veil painted once (`::after`), and collapse the pile by scale alone.
- **Snapping must start where things are.** Compute each photo's on-screen position, rotation and scale at the freeze from the camera, lay a grid tile over it at exactly that transform, then fly (leave the original to collapse underneath: hiding it repaints the whole pile on that frame). Nearest-slot snapping or tiles from nowhere read as a flicker.
- **Too few elements leave holes** that read as a mistake: generate by rule and pad each beat to its count; keep the first two beats hand-placed so the readable cards (and their words) land where the eye is.
- **The accent is rationed.** Red badges and bars are the problem; never colour a problem in the accent, never bring the red back after the turn.
- **Readable at every brand.** The caret and accent words use `--utama-di-latar`, never `--utama`, so a pale yellow brand on white still shows them; cards on a pale stage need their border and shadow.
- **Don't fade.** A flat rectangle for "closing" looks like a placeholder: squash the real surface (CRT-off), retract toasts, put tiles away.
- **Text count.** The mess may carry many tiny words, but what the viewer must read stays within 7 words per screen: label + line, one toast, one number with its unit.

## Measured from the references

The reference runs 12 s at 24 fps: the line types in about 1.0 s (0.07 s per character), the first card slides in at 1.6 s, the pull-back starts around 2.6 s (zoom about 0.6 at 4.5 s, 0.38 at 6.5 s, 0.28 at 8.5 s, 0.2 at the end), a caption every 2 s, notification cards at first about 55 % of the frame wide and a third of it high, three inserts of 0.5-0.7 s with a new value every 0.17 s. This recipe stretches that to 15 s and adds the turn the reference only implies: freeze, snap grid, light reveal, put-away, and the answer typed in the opening framing.

## Variation space

You choose the product's verb, the problem image, the accent, the opening and the ending. Structures: **a countdown** (a checklist ticking through its items, each a UI moment, ending on "selesai"); **side by side** (the old way drowning on the left, the new way finishing early on the right); **a zoom ladder** (one caret → a card → a screen → a wall of screens, each level a new fact). Openings: **the number first** (a huge figure on black, its meaning revealed backwards); **a plan view of an empty grid** filling slot by slot; **an insert storm** from frame one. Endings: **one tile left** lit in the accent; **the product running quietly** in a wide shot; **a single confirmation toast**, then darkness.

# Dark stage talk: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.2, medium 2, long 3.4.

## hook

- en: a mono label and one calm line typed by a glowing accent caret on the dark stage; the caret drops a line and blinks
- id: label mono dan satu kalimat tenang diketik kursor beraksen yang berpendar; kursor turun satu baris lalu berkedip

## problem

- en: generated UI piles in faster and faster (cards slide, files drop, photos fling) while the camera pulls back in log space
- id: kartu, berkas, dan foto menumpuk makin cepat (meluncur, jatuh, dilempar) sementara kamera terus mundur

## fact

- en: one notification card slides in from the edge beside the line; a caption toast with an accent dot names it
- id: satu kartu notifikasi meluncur dari tepi di samping kalimat; toast dengan titik aksen menyebut isinya

## step

- en: one UI card per step flies on a curve into the next grid slot and lands on the beat with a small overshoot
- id: satu kartu UI per langkah terbang melengkung ke slot kisi berikutnya, mendarat tepat di ketukan

## compare

- en: split stage: the old way drowns in spawned cards on one side while the new side stays one quiet card
- id: layar dibelah: cara lama tenggelam dalam tumpukan kartu, sisi baru tetap satu kartu yang tenang

## number

- en: half-second inserts on a gridded stage: a red badge climbs, a giant number scrambles and locks digit by digit
- id: sisipan setengah detik di panggung berkisi: lencana merah naik, angka besar diacak lalu terkunci per digit

## proof

- en: a soft light band sweeps across a window and only the rows it passes turn on; a toast confirms
- id: pita cahaya lembut menyapu jendela dan hanya baris yang dilewatinya menyala; toast mengonfirmasi

## offer

- en: freeze, then everything flies into one grid in a single beat; the grid puts itself away to one accent tile
- id: semua berhenti, lalu terbang ke satu kisi dalam satu ketukan; kisi membereskan diri jadi satu ubin aksen

## cta

- en: back to the opening framing: the accent tile, the name typed by the caret, the contact in a toast, held 2 s
- id: kembali ke bingkai pembuka: ubin aksen, nama diketik kursor, kontak di toast, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: one tile left lit in the accent on an empty stage, the closing line typed beside it, held 2 s
- id: tersisa satu ubin menyala aksen di panggung kosong, kalimat penutup diketik di sampingnya, diam 2 detik

      function foto(seed) { // langit bergradasi, matahari, dua punggung bukit

      // Satu gerak per jenis: kartu meluncur dari tepi, berkas jatuh memantul, foto dilempar berputar, jendela meletup.

      const FOTO = []; // dicatat untuk kisi
      function taruh(b, jenis, html, x, y, rot, q, at, css = "") { // x, y dalam bingkai lebar, dipetakan ke layar tegak
